claims.text: Overall wear resistance and microscopic deformation in FeNiCrCoCu coatings at high temperature are governed by a dynamic, shear-induced near-surface microstructural transformation.
Sliding-induced localized deformation refines an initially coarse coating microstructure into an ultra-nanocrystalline tribolayer.
The sliding-generated tribolayer contains deformation twins and a high dislocation density.
An ultra-nanocrystalline, twinned tribolayer homogenizes the stress distribution.
The refined, twinned tribolayer retards further dislocation slip.
Microstructural refinement at the coating surface decreases wear.
The refined tribolayer minimizes severe localized deformation.
The as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coating has a relatively coarse-grained microstructure.
Rapid post-deposition thermal annealing can pre-induce nanocrystalline grain refinement in the FeNiCrCoCu coating.
Rapid post-deposition thermal annealing can increase the density of deformation twins in the FeNiCrCoCu coating.
Shear-induced dynamic recrystallization occurs during sliding and produces the finely twinned tribolayer.
Pre-existing nanocrystallinity produced by annealing augments shear-induced dynamic recrystallization during sliding.
The refined tribolayer impedes microcrack initiation.
At approximately 500 °C in an inert atmosphere, the annealed coating will have a lower wear rate than the untreated coating.
The annealed coating will exhibit fewer stress-drop events during sliding than the untreated coating.
Using an inert or controlled atmosphere minimizes oxidation effects during testing.
If oxidation or other surface reactions dominate, the proposed wear mechanism may be altered.
The grain refinement and twin density required for optimum wear performance are not quantified.
